summary: Submitted a new Candidate (action=continue) on a genuinely different responsibility, drawn from the previously deferred surface Raft.restoreUserSnapshot. The principal Fact is F-committed (lifecycle consumption) through B-leader-apply, with sourced support from B-quorum-commit (the commitment path is independent of the inflight list), B-apply-api (the client-visible ErrAbortedByRestore signal) and B-config-eligibility (the committedIndex==latestIndex guard). The sourced discrepancy: api.go documents that ErrAbortedByRestore means 'the write effectively failed since its effects will not be present in the FSM after the restore' (new SourceRange S-api-restore-contract, api.go:815-817), while restoreUserSnapshot answers every inflight logFuture with ErrAbortedByRestore and removes it from leaderState.inflight before creating, writing and closing the replacement snapshot; if the injected SnapshotStore's Create/Write/Close fails after that point, the futures already carry the definite 'effectively failed' outcome even though no restore happened and the entries remain in the log and may still be committed and applied. The question asks whether the abort can precede a failed restore and whether those entries are subsequently counted committed and consumed, and it cites the two new sources plus acquired Materials (S-raft-restoresnapshot, S-raft-leaderloop, S-raft-processlogs, S-commitment, S-api-apply, S-raft-configstable). Counterevidence records the configuration guard, the accuracy of the error on the success path, the inflight bookkeeping and the single-shot future response; the remaining unknowns fix the next discriminator (reachability of a post-abort restore failure and whether the client is misinformed). Separately, this run's earlier finding remains confirmed: Finding 30950ca0199d4260b28f48b85bb6c269 is implementation_reproduced with conclusion confirmed_in_scope for the follower log-identity responsibility, and map v2 records it.
